input.body:
Closes #209

## What this is

Research and preparation, no product change. Two commits, one concern each.

**`docs/architecture/claim-similarity.md`** — the research document:

- A review of Heldring & Torres, *Logical Embeddings for Argument Analysis* ([arXiv 2608.15325](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15325)): what it claims, what holds, and what to take. The kernel is sound but modest; the estimator that performs (pairwise, Appendix B.3) is not the PSD one the theory covers; the measure is blind to contradiction by construction; the main text and Definition 20 count differently; the public code repository is a README and a Dropbox link; the cost is O(n²·m²) model calls. What transfers: decompose before comparing, equivalence as judged mutual entailment, keep the clause trail.
- The unit of comparison: **claims** (atomic, decontextualised, keyed on their utterance) for comparison, utterances staying the unit of record.
- A Hebrew-first survey of bi-encoders (BGE-M3, multilingual-e5, Qwen3-Embedding, EmbeddingGemma, OpenAI, Gemini Embedding 2, Cohere, and the Hebrew-only encoders that lack a sentence head), NLI cross-encoders and rerankers (mDeBERTa-2mil7 covers Hebrew; HebNLI's 884-pair gold set; the rerankers' language lists do not name Hebrew), LLM judgment on Workers AI with today's prices, lexical and near-duplicate methods, and Vectorize's limits (1,536 dims, 20M vectors, topK ≤ 100, 50k namespaces) against an all-pairs design that stays linear: `n` embeddings, `n` bounded neighbour queries, cross-encoder on candidates, LLM on the contradictions.
- The comparison protocol (§5): the labelled pair set (five relations, two annotators, hard negatives on purpose), the methods, the metrics (recall@k, MRR, subject separation, per-relation P/R with contradiction recall on its own, extraction faithfulness, cost), and how the corpus-wide run then goes.

**`dev/similarity/`** — the harness that runs that protocol today:

- `pairs.ts` the record format and a reader that refuses a malformed set line by line; `methods.ts` the retriever and pair-judge seams, the lexical baseline, and the adapters a real model plugs into (`Embedder` from the ingestion ports; `PairModel`; the paper's `ClauseModel`); `measure.ts` the paper's syntactic–semantic Jaccard as a pure function, pinned to the paper's own Figure 3 and Figure 4 numbers; `metrics.ts`; `compare.ts` the protocol and the report; `run.ts` the CLI (`npm run similarity:compare`).
- A fictional Hebrew sample set proves the harness and measures no model. The lexical baseline's report on it reads as designed: full retrieval recall on a set this small, contradiction recall 0.
- `compare.test.ts` (12 tests) is in `npm test`. Each metric and the measure were seen to fail under a mutation before being trusted.

## What this does not do

It chooses no model — that is the owner's call on the comparison's real output, which waits on the models being reachable (#27) and on a labelled set of real speech (#32 decides the source). Feeds phase 5 of #34 and gap 3 of #28.

Everything is pushed and the PR is open. Wrapping up with the hand-over.

Done. The work is on [PR #211](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/211), closing [#209](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/209).

**The paper, in short.** *Logical Embeddings for Argument Analysis* defines an argument as premises plus a conclusion and scores two arguments by Jaccard overlap of premises and of the conclusions' CNF consequences, both modulo judged mutual entailment. That measure is a positive semi-definite kernel, so it induces an embedding that loses no logical information. Its framing is exactly this repo's `1.11` problem: cosine distance measures aboutness, not agreement. What does not hold up as well:

- The estimator that produces the reported numbers is the pairwise one, which the PSD theorem does not cover; the PSD variant scores lower.
- The measure is blind to contradiction by construction: a claim and its negation score like two unrelated claims. Its clean pro/con graph is absence of overlap, not detection of conflict.
- The main text and the appendix count the premise overlap differently. The figures use class counting, which is what I implemented and pinned.
- Evaluation is 1,137 English arguments on one task. The public repository is a README and a Dropbox link. Cost is O(n²·m²) model calls.

**What transfers:** decompose utterances into claims before comparing, treat equivalence as a judged relation, and keep the clause trail as the finding's evidence.

**The technology survey** is in [docs/architecture/claim-similarity.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/claude/distance-search-claims-research-nnxydy/docs/architecture/claim-similarity.md), Hebrew first. Key points: BGE-M3, Qwen3-Embedding and EmbeddingGemma are reachable from Workers AI but none has a published Hebrew number. The mDeBERTa NLI cross-encoder was trained with Hebrew, and HebNLI has an 884-pair human-verified gold set. The multilingual rerankers do not list Hebrew. Vectorize caps at 1,536 dimensions, which rules out Gemini Embedding 2 without truncation. The all-pairs design stays linear: embed, bounded nearest-neighbour per persona namespace, cross-encoder on candidates, LLM only on contradictions.

**The comparison** is designed in §5 of the document and runs today in `dev/similarity/` against the lexical baseline and a fictional sample set. Real models plug into the existing `Embedder` port and two new judge ports in one place. Everything else is a config change once [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27) lands.

```
docs/architecture/   the research document: paper review, survey, unit of comparison, comparison protocol
dev/similarity/      the harness: pair-set format, method seams, the paper's measure, metrics, CLI, sample set
package.json         the harness test joins npm test; a similarity:compare script
```

Verification: 109 tests pass, typecheck clean, 0 blocking checks. Each metric and the measure were watched failing under a mutation before being trusted.

Two things for you. The environment's Setup script is missing the Node install step; I ran `npm ci` in-session, but a fresh session will hit the same gap until the body of `.claudinite/shared/packs/claude-code-web-users-support/environment-setup-command.sh` is pasted into the environment's Setup script field. And I can watch the PR for review comments and CI if you want; say so and I'll subscribe.

> ⚠️ Still open: the labelled set of real Hebrew speech (which persona, which two annotators), HebNLI's licence, and the model choice itself, which waits on #27 and the comparison's real output.

   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.
